home:
The **Software Maintenance and Intelligent Evolution** (SMILE) Research Group at the [University of Michigan-Flint](https://umflint.edu/) designs and implements intelligent algorithms to tackle software engineering problems. Our goal is to help developers better maintain and evolve the software systems they depend on.

Our work spans software refactoring, test quality, mining software repositories, search-based software engineering and the use of AI to support developers. We are always glad to hear from motivated students at every level: see [how to join us](/join/).
recruitment:
The SMILE Research Group welcomes motivated bachelor’s, master’s and PhD students who want to do research on how software is built, maintained and evolved. Topics include refactoring, software quality and test smells, mining software repositories, search-based software engineering, and AI for software engineering.

## How to get in touch

Send an email to [Mohamed Wiem Mkaouer](mailto:mmkaouer@umich.edu) with a short introduction, your CV, your unofficial transcript, and a few sentences on the topics that interest you most. Links to your GitHub profile, course projects or papers are welcome. Please mention your current level and when you would like to start.

We read every message, and we reply to candidates whose interests match our current projects.
